skill.name: voice-agents
skill.description: Guides the design of production voice agents, including speech-to-speech and pipeline architectures, latency budgets, turn detection, barge-in handling, and spoken response design.
skill.summary: Design low-latency voice agents with practical architecture, turn taking, and conversation patterns.
skill.author: sickn33

content.value_statement: Voice agent teams must balance latency, turn taking, speech quality, and control. This skill guides architecture choices and production design tradeoffs.
actual_capabilities: Compares speech-to-speech and STT to LLM to TTS pipeline architectures.
Highlights latency as the main design constraint for natural voice conversations.
Covers voice activity detection, turn taking, and barge-in detection patterns.
Calls out anti-patterns such as long responses and silence-only turn detection.
Identifies production concerns like background noise, STT errors, and spoken response format.
limitations: Does not include executable code, SDK examples, or deployment scripts.
Does not evaluate specific vendor pricing, quotas, or current API limits.
Does not provide benchmark data for a concrete application or audio environment.
Requires the user to supply product goals, call flow, and latency targets.

use_cases.title: Voice Agent Architecture Review
use_cases.description: Compare speech-to-speech and pipeline designs before implementation.

use_cases.title: Conversation Flow Planning
use_cases.description: Plan turn taking, barge-in behavior, and short spoken responses for a new agent.

use_cases.title: Production Readiness Checks
use_cases.description: Review latency, noise handling, and STT error risks before launch.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose between speech-to-speech and a pipeline voice agent for [use case]. Compare latency, control, debugging, and user experience.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Turn Taking
prompt_templates.prompt: Design turn taking for a voice agent that handles [conversation type]. Include VAD, interruptions, silence thresholds, and fallback behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Review Latency Budget
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this voice agent architecture for latency risk: [architecture summary]. Identify the slowest components and recommend budget targets.

prompt_templates.title: Create Production Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a production readiness checklist for a voice agent serving [audience]. Cover barge-in, background noise, STT errors, response length, and monitoring.

output_examples.input: Need help choosing speech-to-speech or pipeline for a support agent.
output_examples.output: Recommendation: use speech-to-speech when natural timing and emotional tone matter most. Use a pipeline when auditability, tool control, and debugging matter more.

output: Add semantic voice activity detection for starts and stops.
Support barge-in so users can interrupt long answers.
Define fallback behavior for noise, silence, and overlapping speech.

output_examples.input: Prepare a launch checklist for a voice agent.
output_examples.output: Check latency budgets, response length, background noise handling, STT error recovery, barge-in behavior, and monitoring before release.

best_practices: Start with a clear latency budget for every speech, reasoning, and synthesis step.
Design spoken responses to be short, clear, and easy to interrupt.
Test with noisy audio, overlapping speech, and real user pacing.
anti_patterns: Treating voice as a text chatbot with speech attached.
Using silence-only turn detection for complex conversations.
Allowing long responses that block interruptions and increase latency.

faq.question: What architecture does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers speech-to-speech models and STT to LLM to TTS pipeline designs.

faq.question: Is it focused on a specific vendor?
faq.answer: It mentions OpenAI Realtime API, but the design guidance is broader.

faq.question: Can it generate working code?
faq.answer: The skill is guidance-only. It does not include executable samples or scripts.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Voice AI engineers, product designers, and engineering leads can use it for planning and review.

faq.question: Does it address latency?
faq.answer: Yes. Latency is the central constraint across architecture, turn detection, and response length.

faq.question: Does it cover safety or compliance?
faq.answer: It covers interaction quality risks, but not legal compliance or regulated call handling.
